title: Connexions projectives et uniformisation : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from the previous page): f: X -> S is a proper smooth family of curves with connected fibres of genus g. Notation: omega = Omega^1_{X/S}; Omega = f_*omega is the Hodge bundle; DR = R^1 f_* Omega^._{X/S} is de Rham cohomology. There is the Hodge exact sequence 0 -> Omega -> DR -> Omega^vee -> 0, and an alternating cup-product pairing DR x DR -> O_S for which Omega is Lagrangian. Splittings s: Omega^vee -> DR form a torsor under Hom(Omega^vee, Omega) = Omega (x) Omega. Each splitting s gives an alternating form phi_0 on Omega^vee, i.e. an element of Lambda^2 Omega. Changing s by u changes phi_0 by the antisymmetrisation of u.

This page, line by line:
(1) The condition phi_0 = 0 (the complement s(Omega^vee) is Lagrangian) is linear in u. One gets a torsor sitting in an extension 0 -> Lambda^2 Omega -> Sigma -> O_S -> 0, described as the torsor of 'hyperbolic' (= Lagrangian / symplectic) splittings of DR. The push-out of the splitting torsor along Omega(x)Omega -> Lambda^2 Omega is the Lambda^2 Omega-torsor; the Lagrangian splittings themselves form a torsor under the kernel, Gamma^2 Omega = Sym^2 Omega (char != 2). The next page indeed writes 0 -> Gamma^2 Omega -> Omega(x)Omega -> Lambda^2 Omega -> 0. He notes that this torsor is pulled back from the analogous torsor on the universal (moduli) object for polarized abelian varieties via the period / Torelli map.
(2) For S over T, the Gauss-Manin connection DR -> DR (x) Omega^1_{S/T} does not preserve the Hodge filtration. Its defect (Griffiths transversality, second fundamental form) is an O-linear map Omega -> Omega^vee (x) Omega^1_{S/T}. Equivalently it is the Kodaira-Spencer map V_{S/T} = T_{S/T} -> Omega^vee (x) Omega^vee, which factors through the symmetric square Gamma^2(Omega^vee). He notes it is induced from the corresponding map for polarized abelian varieties. For the universal abelian scheme it is an isomorphism T_{A_g} -> Sym^2 Omega^vee. For the universal curve of genus g it is dual to the multiplication Sym^2 f_*omega -> f_*omega^2 = Omega^1_{S/T}. That map is surjective exactly off the hyperelliptic locus (Max Noether), as the next page records, with kernel of rank (g-2)(g-3)/2.
(3) On the total space X (g >= 2) he considers the absolute/relative differential sequence 0 -> f^*Omega^1_S -> Omega^1_X -> omega_{X/S} -> 0. He relates the resulting filtration and a rank-1 torsor to H^0(X, Omega) and to (DR)_X. This is the start of a comparison between (Lagrangian) splittings of the Hodge filtration and projective structures / projective connections. The next page develops the latter via principal parts P^3: 0 -> omega^2 -> P^3 -> ... and f_*omega^2 = Omega^1_{S/T}, i.e. projective structures form a torsor under the cotangent bundle of moduli.

Overall aim, in line with the folder title: to construct algebraically, over the moduli of curves, a map from the torsor of Lagrangian splittings of H^1_dR (a torsor under Sym^2 Omega) to the torsor of projective connections (a torsor under f_*omega^2 = Omega^1_M). The map is induced by the multiplication Sym^2 Omega -> f_*omega^2. This is the algebraic shadow of the classical Bergman-kernel / Bergman projective connection attached to a Lagrangian complement, and it feeds into uniformization questions.
errors: He writes the torsor of Lagrangian ('hyperbolic') splittings as a torsor under Lambda^2 Omega. From the previous page's formula phi'_0 = phi_0 + (t,u(t')) - (t',u(t)), the Lagrangian splittings form a torsor under the symmetric part Gamma^2 Omega = ker(Omega(x)Omega -> Lambda^2 Omega). Lambda^2 Omega is the group of the push-out torsor / the obstruction space. The page conflates the two, and the next page corrects this by introducing Gamma^2 Omega.

The Kodaira-Spencer map is first written as V_{S/T} -> Omega^vee (x) Omega^vee and then as factoring through a second exterior/divided power. The correct target is the symmetric square (Gamma^2 / Sym^2 Omega^vee), not Lambda^2.
Characteristic 2 is not excluded on this page (it is excluded on the next one). Symmetric vs alternating and Gamma^2 vs Sym^2 matter there.

ideas.what: Polarized Hodge filtration of a curve family: Omega Lagrangian in DR; splittings form an Omega(x)Omega-torsor and Lagrangian splittings a Sym^2 Omega-torsor
ideas.modern_name: Torsor of Lagrangian complements to the Hodge filtration (Siegel-type affine bundle)

ideas.what: Gauss-Manin connection fails to preserve the filtration; the defect is an O-linear map Omega -> Omega^vee (x) Omega^1, i.e. the Kodaira-Spencer map to Sym^2 Omega^vee
ideas.modern_name: Griffiths transversality / second fundamental form / Kodaira-Spencer map of the Hodge bundle
ideas.where_published: Grothendieck's crystalline ideas (Crystals and the de Rham cohomology of schemes, 1966) treat Gauss-Manin; not this specific statement as far as I know

ideas.what: Kodaira-Spencer isomorphism for the universal polarized abelian scheme, and its pull-back along Torelli to M_g; failure of surjectivity of Sym^2 f_*omega -> f_*omega^2 exactly on the hyperelliptic locus
ideas.modern_name: KS isomorphism on A_g; infinitesimal Torelli / Max Noether theorem
ideas.usually_credited_to: Mumford, Faltings-Chai (KS on A_g); Noether, Oort-Steenbrink 1980 (infinitesimal Torelli for M_g)

ideas.what: Comparing the torsor of Lagrangian splittings of H^1_dR with the torsor of projective connections (under f_*omega^2 = Omega^1_M) via the multiplication map Sym^2 Omega -> f_*omega^2
ideas.modern_name: Bergman projective connection attached to a Lagrangian complement; projective structures as an affine bundle over M_g modelled on the cotangent bundle
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical analytic (Bergman, Fay, Tyurin); algebraic: Biswas-Raina, Ben-Zvi-Biswas, Kawai

missed.claim: Grothendieck sets up, purely algebraically over a general base S/T, a comparison between three torsors. The first is the torsor of Lagrangian ('hyperbolic') splittings of the Hodge filtration of H^1_dR. The second is the same torsor pulled back from the universal polarized abelian scheme. The third is the torsor of projective connections, a torsor under f_*omega^2 = Omega^1_{S/T}. The Kodaira-Spencer / Noether multiplication map links them. This anticipates the algebraic treatment of the 'Bergman projective connection from a Lagrangian splitting' and of projective structures as a twisted cotangent bundle over M_g, developed later by others (Biswas-Raina, Ben-Zvi-Biswas and others).
missed.quote: torseur des opérateurs hyperboliques de DR (Il est induit par un torseur analogue sous la solution universelle pour les VA via polarisations)
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: The comparison is known in substance, so the value here is mainly historical: an early, characteristic-free (char != 2) framing linking the Hodge-filtration torsor, the A_g pull-back and uniformization / projective structures. It is unfinished on this page.

deep.surprise_reason: The mathematics (Lagrangian splittings, Griffiths transversality, KS map, Noether's theorem) is standard. The deliberate algebraic linking of Lagrangian-splitting torsors with projective-connection torsors and with A_g, in the context of uniformization, is a nice early framing. However, it is incomplete, partly erroneous (Lambda^2 vs Gamma^2), and its substance appears in later literature.

'(torseurs symplectiques sous Ω ...)' is likely '(structures symplectiques sur Ω ...)'; uncertain.
